name: Ansible
suggestedProbes: Walk me through your largest role or collection — what does it manage?
How do you keep playbooks idempotent? Any war stories where they weren't?
Static or dynamic inventory in production? How do you handle secrets?
How do you test Ansible content before it hits production?
checklistGuidance: Ansible is versionless in practice — what matters is which patterns they actually use. Coverage of roles + inventory + vault + idempotency separates real operators from one-off-script writers.

checklistGuidance: Jenkins is versionless for screening purposes. The signal is whether they treat pipelines as code (declarative + shared libs + JCasC) or as click-ops they barely maintain.

name: GitHub Actions

services.name: OIDC auth to cloud (AWS / Azure / GCP)

checklistGuidance: GitHub Actions is rolling-versioned. Reusable workflows + OIDC + permission scoping is the maturity signal — without those, they probably treat it as a single-file CI runner.

checklistGuidance: GitLab CI is rolling-versioned. DAG + includes + review apps separates engineers who've designed pipelines from those who copy-paste YAML between repos.

name: SQL

checklistGuidance: SQL is dialect-agnostic on paper but candidate depth varies wildly. Coverage of joins, window functions, indexes, and query plans separates real practitioners from copy-paste consumers.

name: C

checklistGuidance: C skill is less about which standard year and more about which concepts and tooling the candidate has internalised. Coverage of memory, pointers, build system, and tooling separates practitioners from CS-class-only knowledge.

name: C++

checklistGuidance: C++ is huge; depth on modern features (C++17 and beyond) signals whether someone has kept up or is still writing C++98-with-classes. Coverage of memory, templates, and tooling matters more than knowing every keyword.
